authors: Akhanov Yerdaulet, Shadiyarbek Syrym, Sabyrzhan Akylbek
rq: How do TomTom and 2GIS traffic-aware travel-time estimates diverge on fixed Astana routes during evening peak compared with off-peak periods?
rq_status: Prospective question; primary collection blocked pending permissions. ORS-only instrument pilot does not answer it.
hypothesis_h1: The magnitude of provider disagreement is greater during evening peak than off-peak periods.
hypothesis_h0: The magnitude of provider disagreement does not differ between periods.
speed_rule_note: Below 2 km/h is a sensitivity screen, not proof of impossible congestion; original rows retained.

tomtom.blocker: Written benchmarking and storage permission not obtained

dgis.blocker: Kazakhstan demo storage and public redistribution rights require confirmation

here.blocker: No API key; billing details required

design_amendments: Provider choice follows verified access and publication terms; original A1 Google/Yandex and A2 Google/2GIS remain historical designs.
20 routes rotate in batches of 4 every 15 minutes: nominal per-route revisit 75 minutes; GitHub schedule delays recorded, not backfilled.
48-hour bounded window replaces 14-day A1 plan because of demo quotas; no quota-increasing retries.
ORS-only pilot tests software and evidence workflow; traffic-aware comparison remains unexecuted.
Same cycle and route with timestamp gap at most 60 seconds define a pair, not a calendar-minute bucket.
Length agreement within 5 percent is only a proxy, not proof of matching route geometry.
